title: AES retry and retention rules
description: Rules are evaluated in file order; the first matching rule wins. Defaults are applied by AES when fields are omitted.

rules.description: An empty array keeps tap logging enabled without automatic retry or cleanup.

seconds.description: Non-negative whole seconds within Go time.Duration range.

consumerFilter.description: '*' matches all consumers; any other value is a Go regex. Use ^...$ for a full match.

event_subject_key.description: An exact subject string, or an object containing a Go regex. A string is never interpreted as a regex.

regex.description: Go regex, compiled by AES at startup. Escape backslashes in JSON.

instance_group.description: Filter selecting the initial delivery's consumer group, not a retry broadcast destination.

instance_name.description: Filter selecting the initial delivery's consumer name. Retry may use another instance in the same group.

try_after.description: Seconds to wait after failure or timeout before retry. 0 disables retry.

try_count.description: Maximum retry attempts, excluding the original delivery. 0 means unlimited; try_after must be positive to enable retry.

consumption_timeout.description: Seconds to wait for a consumption result after delivery. 0 disables the timeout.

on_consumption_timeout.description: keep: retain without automatic action; try: treat as failure and apply retry limits; remove: delete without retry. Ignored when consumption_timeout is 0.

remove_successful_timeout.description: Retention seconds after success, even if the retry limit was not reached. 0 keeps the record indefinitely.

remove_failed_timeout.description: Retention seconds after terminal failure (retry disabled or limit exhausted). Pending retries are not deleted. 0 keeps the record indefinitely.
